scope: Re-screen newly surfaced open-source DWG/DXF routes against the existing peer matrix and statically crosswalk LibreDWG CVE-2026-63474 to libdxfrw's R2004+ data-page allocation lifetime and focused-test coverage.

method.kind: Primary-source project/release review plus read-only local source and test-seam inspection
localInspection: src/intern/dwgreader18.cpp: parseDataPage capacity checks, per-section allocation, page output windows, and post-success publication
src/intern/dwgutil.cpp: dwgCompressor::decompress18 cursor initialization and bounded output path
tests/dwg_reader_matrix_tests.cpp: generated R2004 system-page helper and test-reader parseDataPage override
method.evidenceBoundary: LibreDWG release notes describe a peer implementation failure, not a libdxfrw vulnerability. Local source review finds a structurally different fixed-allocation lifetime but does not prove every malformed input or failure path safe. Mutable peer source/release pages were not pinned to executable artifacts; candidate screening is not exhaustive.

evidence.topic: No newly surfaced candidate qualifies for a new peer gate
observed: ACadRust and OpenCADStudio remain one parser lineage.
uncad documents LibreDWG FFI for DWG and the separately screened undxf route for DXF.
go-cad advertises LibreDWG-derived comparison expectations and retains ACIS/SAB as blobs.
ezdwg remains a bounded read-focused candidate with source/artifact provenance not reconciled.
dwg-rs remains pre-alpha with per-version decoded, skipped, and errored denominators.
Sea-DXF Core says its visible pre-1.0 source is proprietary and is excluded from the open-source comparator set.
evidence.planUse: Retain existing optional route roles and the candidate-discovery stop rule. Add no dependency, routine peer runtime, new gate, or support claim.

evidence.observed: LibreDWG 0.14.1 NEWS reports that read_2004_compressed_section could reset the decompressed logical size to a smaller per-section value while the live cursor and section-data size tracked a larger stream, allowing buffer shrinkage followed by an out-of-bounds write. The release labels this a heap-buffer-overflow write fix and says it completed an earlier mitigation.
doesNotEstablish: an ODA format rule or an implementation to copy
safety of other page, checksum, allocation, or retry paths
evidence.planUse: Keep the mechanism within PAR-14/7BE capacity and lifetime invariants. If a reusable decompression buffer is introduced, test active cursor, logical length, and actual capacity across shrink/grow transitions.

evidence.topic: Local R2004+ data-page path uses a different allocation lifetime
observed: parseDataPage checks page cap/count products and total bounded section capacity before allocating.
A fresh fixed unique_ptr byte array is allocated per section; each page writes through a start-offset pointer with a bounded page output size.
The completed allocation is published to caller state only after every page succeeds.
decompress18 resets its cursor per invocation and bounds writes by the passed output size.
evidence.inference: The exact peer shrink-live-buffer sequence is structurally absent from the inspected path; static inspection is not a general malformed-input safety proof.
evidence.planUse: No new finding or production change. Preserve the fixed-capacity invariant unless a separately reviewed buffer-reuse design is adopted.

evidence.observed: The reviewed test target has a generated R2004 system-page decoder helper, and its test reader overrides parseDataPage to provide prepared section bytes. No dedicated generated control was found that drives differently sized R2004+ data sections through the production parseDataPage implementation and checks complete publication/retry.
evidence.planUse: Conditionally add one selector to the existing reader-matrix target when the data-page production path is next modified. Generate a multi-page section followed by a smaller section; assert exact logical lengths and sentinels. Corrupt a later page and assert no partial publication and same-reader retry. Avoid a new CTest registration or committed fixture. If full parser synthesis is not cheap, test the narrow capacity helper and explicitly retain the integration-coverage limitation.

nextActions: Continue the current local implementation queue; peer discovery and the deferred test do not block unrelated slices.

If the R2004+ data-page decoder or allocation lifetime is next changed, add the smallest generated selector under the existing reader-matrix target to exercise differently sized data sections and failure/retry publication.
Do not infer a local vulnerability from CVE-2026-63474 or add a peer dependency, fixture, full-suite run, sanitizer run, or native application gate for this research update.
Keep J256, J260, J268, J284, J293, and J295 DEFERRED_EXTERNAL and non-promoting.
